previous_description: Aggregate of application components working together
definition: An active structure element that names a grouping of two or more application components (or nested collaborations) which jointly perform collective behaviour. It is a logical or configured grouping of independently deployable parts, not a deployable unit or behaviour in its own right.

distinguish_from.when: the symbol is a single modular, deployable unit, even if it internally composes sub-modules or calls other services
the symbol describes the joint behaviour itself, such as a message exchange, saga step sequence or protocol between components, rather than the group of participants
the symbol is an ordered sequence of steps that achieves a result, even if those steps span several components
the symbol is the externally exposed functionality the group offers rather than the group of participating components

code_evidence: a saga or choreography definition (e.g. Temporal/Camunda workflow config, event-flow manifest) that enumerates several named participating services under one collective name
a docker-compose file, Helm umbrella chart or Kubernetes namespace that groups multiple separately built services as one named subsystem delivering a shared capability
an architecture document, ADR or C4 diagram boundary that names a set of cooperating services (e.g. 'checkout subsystem: cart, pricing, payment') as a unit

attribute_descriptions.name: documentation
attribute_descriptions.description: A free-text description of the collaboration that names its participating components and the joint purpose they serve. Set it whenever the element name alone does not make membership or purpose clear.

notes: Rarely maps to a single code symbol, so a classifier will seldom match it from a state card. ArchiMate assigns a collaboration to an interaction, but the spec models this as depends-on/delivers-value; consider an 'assigned-to' relationship. The parallel aggregates and depends-on links to applicationcomponent are redundant. A 'members' or minimum-cardinality constraint is missing.
